---
title: "Handle failed and stopped prompts"
sidebarTitle: "Failed prompts"
description: "How Agent SDK reports a failed or stopped prompt, why it adds nothing to the history, and how to resend the prompt or return it to the user."
keywords: ["error", "cancelled", "retry", "failed prompt"]
---

A prompt that errors or is stopped adds nothing to the history, not even the prompt itself. The `error` event carries the prompt, so your plugin can send it again or hand it back to the user.

```lua
on = {
  error = function(event)
    if event.cancelled then
      return restore_input(event.prompt)
    end
    vim.notify(event.message, vim.log.levels.ERROR)
    last_failed_prompt = event.prompt
  end,
}

session:prompt(last_failed_prompt)
```

`restore_input` is your plugin's own function, putting the prompt back in its input buffer.

## The error event

| Field | |
| --- | --- |
| `event.message` | What went wrong |
| `event.cancelled` | `true` when your plugin stopped the reply |
| `event.prompt` | What was passed to `session:prompt()` |

## When an agent's process exits

If an ACP agent's process exits, its history goes with it. The prompt in progress ends in an `error`, and so does every later prompt in that session. Start a new session to carry on.
